# PromptPack

> PromptPack (promptpack.tech) is a digital shop run by Ornalens LLP, India. It sells editable AI prompt packs and illustrated PDF field guides for websites, personal finance, social media, video and design. 12 products have purchase routes, including 10 complete guide editions with free sample prompts.

Updated: 2026-10-18. All products are digital downloads used with the buyer's own AI tools. They do not include AI credits, software subscriptions, recorded courses or publishing services.

## Available now

- [Money Audit Pack](https://promptpack.tech/finance): Find recurring charges in your billing emails. Turn them into a Keep / Review / Compare / Negotiate action plan with your AI assistant. Gmail setup + audit prompts + review worksheets. US$19, or ₹1,599 · one time.
- [75+ Website Prompts](https://promptpack.tech/products/website-prompts/): Website briefs for landing pages, portfolios, SaaS and 3D-style sites. Choose a motion reference, edit the brief and build in your own AI tool. Markdown prompts + motion references. US$8.50, one-time purchase.

## Digital guide details

### Carousel Studio

URL: https://promptpack.tech/products/carousel-studio/
Category: Social content
Status: available through Razorpay checkout for ₹699 (UPI, Indian cards, netbanking or wallets) or US$12 (international cards), paid once
Format: 13-page illustrated PDF guide, 12 editable prompts, worked example, starter files, worksheets

A reference-led system for six-slide carousels with a cover that earns the swipe. Six connected slides with a strong cover, relevant imagery and one practical next action, plus the caption, alt text and source ledger. The guide teaches the visual decisions; the staged prompts carry them through research, style lock, storyboard, image prompts and review.

For: Creators, marketers and small business owners who publish educational or news carousels.
Requirements: A text AI assistant and an image generator (ideally one that accepts reference images), or a design editor for art-plus-typesetting. Image tools, accounts and credits are separate.
Scope: Image generation needs your own tool, account and credits. The optional starter renderer only checks text fit with a simple typography template; it does not generate illustrations or publish. No social account access or scheduling is included, and the examples show an editorial process, not guaranteed reach or engagement.

Workshop steps:
1. Choose one reader and one job
2. Study references as a designer
3. Lock a system, not six layouts
4. Make the cover earn the swipe
5. Write a complete image prompt
6. Review the output, not the prompt

First session:
1. Read GUIDE.pdf, then fill MASTER-BRIEF.md and collect verified source notes.
2. Study references with REFERENCE-WORKSHEET.csv, then plan every slide in WORKSHEET.csv.
3. Run the staged prompts in PROMPTS.md: choose an angle, lock the visual system and storyboard six slides.
4. Generate one cover in your image tool, check it at phone size, then generate the interiors and review them with QUALITY-CHECKLIST.md.

Public tools referenced: python-pillow/Pillow (MIT-CMU (stated in upstream LICENSE; GitHub detected NOASSERTION)) https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow; microsoft/playwright (Apache-2.0) https://github.com/microsoft/playwright; Jakeschincariol/instagram-agent-skill (MIT) https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/instagram-agent-skill

Sample prompt:

Create a reusable style block for [APPROVED ANGLE + BRAND + REFERENCES]. Specify canvas and safe zone, palette roles with hex values, headline/body/metadata hierarchy, image medium, material, light direction, texture, connectors, source/page-marker positions and avoid list. State what remains consistent and what varies. Offer one recommended direction, then repeat its style block verbatim for use in every slide prompt. Do not treat one creator's profile as one universal visual style.

Direct an original amber-lantern concept through changes in framing without mistaking attractive stills for working video.

For: Creators and small production teams planning AI-assisted visual sequences.
Requirements: Rights-cleared references, an image/video tool with known controls, credits where required and an editor.
Scope: Visual treatment and directing workflow, not finished video or a generation service. Provider access, credits, editing software, soundtrack and any real production are separate. Exact continuity is not guaranteed. The Python/Pillow starter creates a symbolic planning sheet; model weights and a production editing project are not included.

Workshop steps:
1. Choose an observable visual promise
2. Make a reference and continuity contract
3. Give camera and subject separate jobs
4. Adapt the prompt to the production route
5. Choose takes by continuity before beauty
6. Deliver a cut-ready direction package

First session:

2. Approve one subject reference and lock geometry, material, light and camera axis.
3. Use the staged prompts to prototype one camera move, record actual model settings and inspect the complete clip.
4. Select takes through the continuity gate and give an editor matching shot IDs, usable ranges, rights notes and the edit map.

Public tools referenced: huggingface/diffusers (Apache-2.0) https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers

Using [SUBJECT FACTS OR FICTIONAL INPUTS], [RIGHTS-CLEARED REFERENCES] and [DURATION BUDGET], define one visible promise, six shot jobs and the final attention target. Separate product facts from styling. State what cannot be claimed from concept art. Do not imitate a named filmmaker or invent a real product capability.

Use a two-gate metaphor to explain the fictional rule that approval and due time are separate conditions.

Workshop steps:

4. Choose the production route
5. Review comprehension and captions
6. Deliver the explanation with its limits

### Juno & Pixel

URL: https://promptpack.tech/products/motion-with-code/
Category: Video
Status: available through Razorpay checkout for ₹1,499 (UPI, Indian cards, netbanking or wallets) or US$29 (international cards), paid once
Format: 16-page illustrated PDF guide, 20 editable prompts, worked example, starter files, worksheets

Two-character 3D reels from a 100-word script, made entirely in code. Write a short two-character script and render a voiced, captioned vertical reel on your own computer. Use the included engine, ten original episodes and four reusable formats, then reskin a working copy for your own brand.

For: Creators and small businesses comfortable running local tools who want an original recurring character series.
Requirements: A computer, Node.js 20+, Python 3.10+, free local model/browser downloads and time to test and render. Coding assistance is useful for a new mascot.
Scope: The core uses free local tools after downloading models and a browser. You supply a computer, setup time, storage and electricity; rendering is not instant. Models, Python/Node runtimes and HyperFrames are installed separately. Ten new scripts are format-validated, not ten rendered movies. No MP4, paid API, hosting, publishing service or audience result is included.

Workshop steps:
1. Build a repeatable two-character show
2. Set up the free local production route
3. Direct voices, emotions and eyes
4. Choose the camera for the beat
5. Show proof and reskin the brand
6. Review, render and publish deliberately

First session:
1. Install the free local runtime, voice/model cache and browser, then run the script validator.
2. Inspect one original episode and its factual source; keep the supplied engine unchanged.
3. Prepare with the explicit-Parakeet wrapper, preview, then render one full episode on your computer.
4. Review the actual movie, measure its end-card hold and publish separately with one real CTA.

Public tools referenced: heygen-com/hyperframes (Apache-2.0) https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes

Sample prompt:

Create an original two-character series bible for [AUDIENCE] about [TOPIC RANGE]. Juno supplies a short problem and Pixel supplies a calm, bounded fix. Define character jobs, palette, end card, proof-panel rules and one CTA per episode. Openings must be eight words or fewer. Reject copied mascots, creator jokes, real-person impersonation and invented performance claims. Return a reusable bible plus five testable episode premises.

Workshop steps:

5. Review the clip through time
6. Make a reusable selected-shot menu

First session:

2. Shortlist three candidates, approve the subject reference and translate the visual system.

Public tools referenced: huggingface/diffusers (Apache-2.0) https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers
